name: NewWork Aoto
card: A small 13-seat site on the 4th floor of the Asahi Life Katsushika Building, five minutes from Aoto Station
title: NewWork Aoto — a small 13-seat corporate-membership satellite office on the 4th floor of the Asahi Life Katsushika Building
lead: NewWork Aoto is on the 4th floor of the Asahi Life Katsushika Building, a five-minute walk from Aoto Station. It is a small site with 13 open and booth seats, a meeting room for 6 and three single-person seated booths. It is a corporate-membership satellite shared office run by Tokyu Corporation. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Tokyu Corporation (corporate membership only; no drop-in)
13 seats (open / booth) / 1 meeting room for 6 / 3 seated single-person booths
concept: A small workplace close to where people live
NewWork Aoto is a small site with 13 seats. It is made up of open and booth seats, one meeting room for 6 and three single-person seated booths.
The official website explains, with a diagram, that the way you enter and leave the building changes after 18:00. It is worth checking before using it in the evening.
steps: There are 13 seats of two kinds: open and booth.
The printer is free, and there is Wi-Fi, power and phone booths.
Three single-person seated booths are available by booking.
To keep using one beyond 120 minutes, you make a new booking.
There is one meeting room for 6, booked in advance.
After 18:00, follow the official website's instructions for entering and leaving the building.

word.title: What is drop-in?
body: Using a space for a single day and paying just for that, without becoming a member.
Because NewWork works on corporate membership, the official website states that drop-in use is not available.

name: H¹T Shibuya Miyamasuzaka
card: 14 private rooms and 5 meeting rooms on the 8th floor of Wako Miyamasuzaka
title: H¹T Shibuya Miyamasuzaka — a corporate shared office with 14 private rooms and 5 meeting rooms on the 8th floor of Wako Miyamasuzaka
lead: H¹T Shibuya Miyamasuzaka (formerly H¹T Shibuya), run by Nomura Real Estate, is on the 8th floor of Wako Miyamasuzaka on the Miyamasuzaka slope, a three-minute walk from Shibuya Station on the Ginza, Hanzomon and Fukutoshin lines and the Tokyu lines. H¹T is a shared office for companies with no initial or base fee. This site has 14 single-person rooms and five meeting rooms for 2 to 6, and is open 7:30–20:00 on weekdays, Saturdays and holidays. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Open space for 10 / 14 single rooms / meeting rooms: 2 for 2, 2 for 4, 1 for 6
JR Shibuya Station 4 min walk / Tokyo Metro & Tokyu Shibuya Station 3 min / Keio Inokashira Line Shibuya Station 3 min
concept: A Shibuya site with plenty of meeting rooms
H¹T Shibuya Miyamasuzaka has five meeting rooms — two for 2, two for 4 and one for 6 — so you can choose a room by headcount.

H¹T is Nomura Real Estate's satellite shared office for companies, and the official website describes it as usable for many purposes: remote work, a base for sales staff out on the road, seminars, training and interviews.
steps: It is handy for checking email or polishing documents before or after meetings in Shibuya.
With a door to close, you can take online meetings and calls without worrying about those around you.
The meeting rooms are two for 2, two for 4 and one for 6.
They cover everything from client interviews to team meetings.

word.title: What is Miyamasuzaka?
body: The name of the slope that rises from the east side of Shibuya Station towards Aoyama.
H¹T Shibuya Miyamasuzaka is on the 8th floor of Wako Miyamasuzaka on this slope, and was previously called “H¹T Shibuya”.

credits: H¹T (Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.)

name: H¹T Akasaka-mitsuke
card: One minute from Exit 10 of Akasaka-mitsuke Station, open on Sundays and holidays too
title: H¹T Akasaka-mitsuke — a corporate shared office on the 7th floor of No.R Akasaka-mitsuke, one minute from the station and open Sundays and holidays
lead: H¹T Akasaka-mitsuke, run by Nomura Real Estate, is on the 7th floor of No.R Akasaka-mitsuke, a one-minute walk from Exit 10 of Akasaka-mitsuke Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza and Marunouchi lines. H¹T is a shared office for companies with no initial or base fee. This site is open 7:30–20:30 on weekdays and Saturdays, and 7:30–17:30 on Sundays and holidays. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Open space for 12 / 5 single boxes / 8 single rooms / meeting rooms: 2 for 2, 1 for 6
Ginza & Marunouchi lines Akasaka-mitsuke Station Exit 10, 1 min walk / Chiyoda Line Akasaka Station Exit 1, 7 min
concept: In Akasaka, convenient and well known
The official website presents this site as a satellite shared office in the Akasaka area that “combines convenience and name recognition”.
It has 12 open-space seats, five single-person boxes, eight single-person rooms and three meeting rooms, and stays open until 17:30 on Sundays and holidays.
steps: One minute from the station exit, it is easy to drop in between appointments.
There are five single-person boxes and eight single-person rooms.
A box suits times when you want some screening from view; a room suits calls and online meetings.
Two rooms for 2 and one for 6
The meeting rooms are two for 2 and one for 6.
They work for meetings with clients in Akasaka and small-group discussions.

word.title: What is an H¹T “box”?
body: One of H¹T's seat types: a single-person seat with surrounding panels. It sits between a “room”, a private room with a door, and the “open space”.
H¹T Akasaka-mitsuke has five single-person boxes.

credits: H¹T (Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.)

name: H¹T Toranomon
card: Directly linked to Exit 10 of Toranomon Station, with 27 private rooms on the 9th floor
title: H¹T Toranomon — a corporate shared office with 27 private rooms, directly linked to the station on the 9th floor of the Toranomon Jitsugyo Kaikan
lead: H¹T Toranomon, run by Nomura Real Estate, is on the 9th floor of the Toranomon Jitsugyo Kaikan main building, directly linked to Exit 10 of Toranomon Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line. H¹T is a shared office for companies with no initial or base fee. This site has as many as 27 single-person rooms and is open 7:00–22:30 on weekdays and 7:00–17:30 on Saturdays. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Weekdays 7:00–22:30 / Sat 7:00–17:30 / closed Sundays and holidays
5 single boxes / 27 single rooms / meeting rooms: 1 for 2, 1 for 3, 2 for 8
Ginza Line Toranomon Station 1 min walk (linked to Exit 10) / Kasumigaseki Station 4 min / Mita Line Uchisaiwaicho Station 5 min
concept: A station-linked base for people in sales
The official website recommends this site for “sales staff who rush around the central business district”.
There is no open space: it has five single-person boxes, 27 single-person rooms and four meeting rooms — a layout built around seats where you can shut yourself away and work.
steps: They suit short tasks or waiting for your next appointment.
With a door to close, you can take online meetings and calls without worrying about those around you.
There is one meeting room each for 2 and 3, and two for 8.
They also work for meetings with clients in Kasumigaseki or Uchisaiwaicho.

word.title: What is an H¹T “room”?
body: One of H¹T's seat types: a single-person private room with a door, suited to online meetings and phone calls.
H¹T Toranomon has 27 of them.

credits: H¹T (Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.)

name: BasisPoint Jimbocho
card: A hotel-lounge-style 6th floor, one minute from Exit A5 of Jimbocho Station
title: BasisPoint Jimbocho — a hotel-lounge-style coworking space on the 6th floor of the Kurosawa Building, one minute from Jimbocho Station
lead: BasisPoint Jimbocho is on the 6th floor of the Kurosawa Building, a one-minute walk from Exit A5 of Jimbocho Station. The official website calls it “a refined space like a hotel lounge”. An open space with tables, a counter and sofas is joined by single-person booths, BOX seats with monitors and two meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Jimbocho Station Exit A5, 1 min walk
Open space / private booths A & B (1 person) / BOX seats (1–4) / meeting rooms Room.A (10) and Room.B (8)
Weekdays 8:00–22:00 / weekends & holidays 10:00–22:00 (closed over New Year)
hero_cap: The open space at BasisPoint Jimbocho
concept: A place like a hotel lounge
Every BasisPoint location aims to be “a refined space like a hotel lounge”. The Jimbocho site is presented as a place where you can focus comfortably and also hold business meetings.
The open space has three kinds of seating — tables, a counter and sofas. It is a workspace that individuals and companies alike can use to suit their needs.
steps: Open seats cost ¥330 for the first 30 minutes, with a daily cap of ¥3,300. Monthly plans start at ¥27,500.
Every seat has Wi-Fi and power.
Seats to hide away in, and seats to talk
BOX seats with monitors are for 1–4 people. There are two single-person booths, A and B.
They suit web meetings and small-group discussions.
A BOX seat with a monitor
There are two meeting rooms: Room.A (10 people, 16.77 m²) and Room.B (8 people, 10.62 m²).
One minute from the station, it is easy to direct visitors here.

word.title: What is drop-in?
body: Using a seat just for the day without becoming a member. BasisPoint Jimbocho starts at ¥330 for the first 30 minutes.
With a daily cap of ¥3,300, it works for a short stop or a whole day.

name: BasisPoint Shimbashi Ginzaguchi
card: One minute from the Ginza Exit of Shimbashi Station, with large rooms for up to 56
title: BasisPoint Shimbashi Ginzaguchi — a coworking space with large rooms for up to 56, one minute from the Ginza Exit of Shimbashi Station
lead: BasisPoint Shimbashi Ginzaguchi is on the 2nd floor of the Kashikei Building, a one-minute walk from the Ginza Exit of JR Shimbashi Station. Along with an open space, sofa seats, private booths and BOX seats, it has three meeting rooms and two large “Lab.” rooms that each hold 56 people. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Shimbashi Station Ginza Exit, 1 min walk
Open space / sofa seats / private booths / BOX seats / 3 meeting rooms (6, 10, 12; B+C combined for 25) / large rooms Lab.A and Lab.B (56 each)
Weekdays 8:00–22:00 / weekends & holidays 10:00–22:00 (closed over New Year)
hero_cap: The open space at BasisPoint Shimbashi Ginzaguchi
concept: From solo work to seminars
Shimbashi Ginzaguchi is another BasisPoint location built around “a refined space like a hotel lounge”. Fast Wi-Fi and power at every seat support remote work and web meetings.
What sets it apart is the range of room sizes: from a single-person booth to a combined meeting room for 25 and large rooms for 56, all in one place.
steps: A lounge one minute from the station
Open seats cost ¥330 for the first 30 minutes, with a daily cap of ¥3,300. Monthly plans range from ¥12,100 to ¥27,500.
There are also sofa seats for four.
BOX seats with monitors are for 1–4 people and cost ¥1,980 per hour. There are three private booths: A, B and C.
Seats for focusing alone and seats for talking in small groups are kept separate.
A BOX seat with a monitor
There are three meeting rooms: Room.A (6), Room.B (10) and Room.C (12). B and C can be joined for 25.
From sales meetings to internal meetings, you can choose a room by headcount.
There are two large rooms, Lab.A and Lab.B, each holding 56 people.
They can host seminars, study sessions and other large events.

word.title: What is a combinable meeting room?
body: Two neighbouring meeting rooms whose partition can be opened so they work as one large room. At BasisPoint Shimbashi Ginzaguchi, Room.B and Room.C can be joined for 25 people.
They stay as small rooms day to day and become one big room only when needed.

name: BasisPoint Ikebukuro
card: One minute from the East Exit of Ikebukuro Station, with talking and web meetings allowed at every seat
title: BasisPoint Ikebukuro — a coworking space on the 4th floor of the Fukano Building where every seat allows conversation, one minute from the East Exit
lead: BasisPoint Ikebukuro is on the 4th floor of the Fukano Building, a one-minute walk from the East Exit of JR Ikebukuro Station. The official website says its “refined space like a hotel lounge” allows conversation and web meetings at every seat. An open space with tables, a counter and sofas is joined by BOX seats, private booths and a meeting room for 10. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: JR Ikebukuro Station East Exit, 1 min walk
Open space (tables, counter, sofas) / BOX seats (1–4) / private booth (1 person) / meeting room (10)
hero_cap: The open space at BasisPoint Ikebukuro
concept: A lounge where you can talk at every seat
The Ikebukuro site clearly states that talking and web meetings are fine at every seat. With no seats where you must keep quiet, it suits people who make lots of calls or hold meetings.
Small extras are covered too: free drinks (coffee, tea, water), blankets and phone chargers.
steps: Open seats cost ¥330 for the first 30 minutes, with a daily cap of ¥3,300.
Sofa seats are available at ¥1,980 per hour.
BOX seats with monitors are semi-private spaces for 1–4 people. The private booth is a fully enclosed room for one, at ¥600 per 30 minutes.
You can switch seats depending on whether you need to talk or to focus.
A BOX seat with a monitor
The meeting room holds 10 people and measures 13.94 m². It costs ¥1,980 per 30 minutes (minimum one hour).
One minute from the station, it is easy to direct visitors here.

word.title: What is a BOX seat?
body: A semi-private seat enclosed by partitions. At BasisPoint Ikebukuro, BOX seats have monitors and fit 1–4 people.
Less closed-off than a private room, but calmer for conversation than an open seat — somewhere in between.

name: HAPON Shinjuku
card: A table shaped like the Japanese archipelago, and a tatami room called “Fuji”
title: HAPON Shinjuku — a shared office themed on “Japan”, with an archipelago-shaped table and a tatami room, on the 5th floor of the Musashi Building
lead: HAPON Shinjuku is on the 5th floor of the Musashi Building in Nishi-Shinjuku 7-chome. Its theme is “Japan”. A shared table shaped like the Japanese archipelago, a tatami meeting space called the “Fuji Room”, a café space and bookshelves fill a shared office covering the whole 419.41 m² floor. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Open space (archipelago-shaped shared table, tatami “Fuji Room”, café space, bookshelves) / South meeting room (about 8) / North meeting room (about 8) / reception room (about 5)
concept: Hap on!
HAPON's concept is “Hap on!” — the name carries the idea that work is all about chance encounters.
The official website describes it as a shared office themed on “Japan”, creating a place where people from many industries meet. The archipelago-shaped table turns that idea directly into furniture.
steps: Sit on the map of Japan
At the centre of the open space is a shared table shaped like the Japanese archipelago.
It is a playful piece of furniture where conversation might start with which region of Japan you happen to be sitting on.
There is a tatami meeting space called the “Fuji Room”, where you take your shoes off to talk.
A café space and bookshelves are also part of the open space.
The South and North meeting rooms each hold about 8 people, and the reception room about 5.
Shared areas and closed rooms sit together on the same floor.

word.title: What does “Hap on!” mean?
body: The concept phrase of HAPON Shinjuku. The official website explains that it carries the meaning “work is all about chance encounters”.
Creating encounters between people from many industries is what the space sets out to do.

name: co-lab Daikanyama
card: A creators' shared office on floors 4–6 of SodaCCo, with a terrace and rooftop
title: co-lab Daikanyama — a shared office for creators on floors 4–6 of SodaCCo, with a terrace and rooftop
lead: Walk along Hachiman-dori from Daikanyama Station to near Namikibashi, and co-lab Daikanyama occupies the 4th to 6th floors of SodaCCo. With 15 rooms, 16 booths, 9 desks, flexible seats, five meeting rooms, a terrace and a rooftop, it is a shared office for creators. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 15 rooms (3–25 people) / 16 booths (1–2) / 9 desks (1) / Flex / 5 meeting rooms / terrace and rooftop
concept: Creative education for children
co-lab Daikanyama's mission is “creative education for children, drawing on the collective knowledge of creators and the local community”.

The official website describes a cycle: developing educational programmes and products for the next generation to nurture children's creativity, while children's imagination and curiosity bring fresh perspectives to the creators' own work.
steps: The building is SodaCCo, and reception is on the 4th floor.
In front of reception is a shared area where members run into each other.
Seats for one, seats for two
Desks are for one person from ¥35,000 a month; booths for 1–2 people start at ¥60,000 a month. Flex seats start at ¥15,000 a month.
The 4th floor also has a large meeting room.
The large meeting room on the 4th floor
Rooms with a terrace, and a rooftop
There are 15 rooms for 3–25 people. On the 6th floor, some rooms face a terrace.
The building also has a rooftop where you can spend time in the open air.

word.title: What is Flex?
body: One of co-lab's membership types: a single-person seat with no fixed place. At co-lab Daikanyama it starts at ¥15,000 a month.
Seat types step up from Flex to desks, booths and rooms.

name: co-lab Gotanda with JPRE
card: “When makers gather, the city changes” — a creators' base with a sauna
title: co-lab Gotanda with JPRE — a shared office for creators, with a sauna, on the 2nd floor of the Gotanda JP Building
lead: co-lab Gotanda with JPRE is on the 2nd floor of the Gotanda JP Building. Its motto is “When makers gather, the city changes”. Along with rooms, ateliers, studios and booths, it has nine meeting rooms, eleven online booths, an event space — and even a sauna. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: 3 rooms (33–36 people) / 6 ateliers (8–16) / 7 studios (16) / 10 booths (1–4) / Flex / 9 meeting rooms / 11 online booths / sauna / event space
concept: When makers gather, the city changes
The motto of co-lab Gotanda with JPRE is “When makers gather, the city changes”. As a collaborative shared office just for creators, it is building a place in Gotanda where makers come together.
It stands out for its range of room types: from rooms for up to 36 to ateliers, studios and booths for 1–4, so teams can choose by size.
steps: Past reception, the open space and shared areas open up.
Flex seats start at ¥22,000 a month.
There are nine meeting rooms, and the official website also shows project rooms.
Eleven online booths are available for web meetings.
There are seven studios for 16 and six ateliers for 8–16.
There are also ten booths for 1–4 people, from ¥64,000 a month.
There is a sauna inside the facility.
It is a place to warm up and reset your mind between tasks.

word.title: What is an atelier?
body: Originally a word for a painter's or craftsperson's workshop. At co-lab Gotanda with JPRE, it is the name of a room type for 8–16 people.
Giving distinct names to rooms, ateliers, studios and booths is a touch that suits a space made for creators.
